answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing tasks that a randomly assigned peer later verifies against the submitted work; a verifier’s own score rises when its judgments match independent audits. To make a sybil swarm count, an attacker must fund many accounts, produce useful outputs, and avoid colluding verification patterns that audits expose. That makes fake identities costly in labor and capital, not just cheap email addresses. A willow-shaped network may hide links briefly, but each relic account still has to pass through the same spiral of work and scrutiny.
